Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.



If you'd like to build the world's best AI cloud, join us.





*Note: This position requires presence in our Bellevue or San Francisco office location 4 days per week; Lambda’s designated work from home day is currently Tuesday.



Lambda, The Superintelligence Cloud, is a leader in AI cloud infrastructure serving tens of thousands of customers. Our customers range from AI researchers to enterprises and hyperscalers. Lambda's mission is to make compute as ubiquitous as electricity and give everyone the power of superintelligence. One person, one GPU.



Every customer workload on Lambda depends on the network, from a single-GPU experiment to a training run spanning thousands of GPUs. When an optic degrades, a link flaps or a switch fails, customers feel it as stalled jobs, restarts and lost compute time. We will operate the existing network flawlessly for all customer workloads while we reinvent how failures are found and fixed, and the automation underneath all of it.



Lambda has 10x'd over the last three years, and the network engineering organization is scaling to match. We're looking for a Senior Director of Network Reliability Engineering to own the health of that network end to end: the break-fix operations that restore service today, and the software that detects, isolates and repairs failures automatically so that most never reach a human or a customer.



You'll lead an organization spanning network SRE and automation engineering, incident management, and break-fix coordination with our data center teams. We're looking for an experienced leader of leaders who treats every repeated failure as a software problem, measures reliability and builds toward a self-healing network where detection, diagnosis and remediation run as automated closed loops. You'll hire and grow a talented team of software and network proficient engineers, shape team culture, and partner with technical leadership to keep reliability ahead of our scale ambitions.



This role will report to the VP of Cloud and AI Networking, working alongside a highly capable and passionate team of engineers. If you'd like to join a great team of customer obsessed engineers building the world's best AI cloud, come join us.


What You'll Do

 - Own the reliability of Lambda's network end to end, from GPU compute fabrics to data center, backbone and edge, and be accountable for availability, time to detect and time to restore

 - Run break-fix operations at scale: fault detection, triage, hardware replacement and RMA, optics and cabling remediation, and coordination with Data Center Operations and remote-hands partners across a growing fleet of data centers

The role sits within a horizontal Market Data platform organization responsible for delivering accurate, deterministic, and low‑latency market data to a broad set of internal consumers, including Electronic Execution (Algo/SOR), Market Access, and analytics platforms.

It all started when engineer Fred Luddy wrote code that automated a tedious task for his coworker, Phyllis. She cried tears of joy. That moment inspired Fred to build a company that could do that for everyone—freeing people from busywork so they could focus on meaningful work. Today, ServiceNow is the AI control tower for business reinvention. Our ServiceNow AI platform brings together any AI, any data, and any workflow— helping 85% of the Fortune 500® work smarter, faster, and better. We're building an AI-native culture where technology and talent are unstoppable together. And we're just getting started.
Join us to put AI to work for people.

The Role
The AI Control Tower is ServiceNow's central hub for governing every AI model, agent, and dataset across the enterprise. We're building the infrastructure that enterprises will depend on as agentic AI moves from experiment to production — and we need a Director of Engineering who has been in that position before: shipping a 1.0 product, fighting for its first users, and figuring out how to turn early traction into durable adoption.
This isn't a role for someone who has managed mature systems. It's for someone who has built something from scratch — in a small, fast company where there was no playbook — and who is now ready to do it at the scale and ambition of ServiceNow. Reporting to the VP of Engineering, AICT, you will lead one or more product areas within the AICT platform, with scope and ownership evolving as the product and team grow.
You are AI-native. You don't just understand AI conceptually — you use it daily, you build with it, and you bring that instinct into how your team designs and ships.

What You Will Do
Product Delivery & Roadmap Execution Own the engineering roadmap for your AICT product areas — translating product requirements into technical plans, managing delivery across a focused engineering team, and maintaining the velocity needed to meet the demands of a fast-moving market. You have done this before and know the difference between motion and progress.
1.0 to Adoption Drive the full arc from early release to meaningful customer adoption. You understand that shipping a 1.0 is only half the job — the other half is learning fast, iterating based on what real customers do (not what they say), and building the feedback loops that compound adoption over time.
AI-Native Engineering Set the standard for how your team uses AI in its own development practice — from AI-assisted code review and testing to designing platform features that assume AI agents are first-class users. You lead by example: your team should see you using AI tools as fluently as you use a terminal.
Team Building Recruit, develop, and retain a high-performing engineering team. You are a strong technical voice who can also grow engineers — you give clear feedback, create stretch opportunities, and build the kind of team culture that makes people want to stay and do their best work.

- Design and maintain an effective control environment across data and AI platforms, identifying, assessing, and mitigating operational, regulatory, privacy, cyber, model, and technology risks

Position Summary
CVS Health is seeking a highly motivated and experienced network leader to join our Infrastructure Operations & Service Delivery organization as the Lead Director - Network Core Infrastructure Operations. You will lead the engineers who keep our core routing and switching environment running - infrastructure that spans over 10,000 applications (approximately 4,100 cloud-hosted), serves 190,000 users, encompasses 10,000+ locations, and includes multiple datacenters and multi-cloud environments.
As the Lead Director – Network Core Infrastructure Operations, you will be accountable for the stability, performance, and security of the company's WAN and LAN, the core network services (DNS, DHCP, and IPAM) that everything else depends on, and the day-to-day operations of a Level 1–3 network operations team. This is a deliberately balanced leadership role: we are looking for a leader who still knows the technology deeply and can go hands-on when it matters, while coaching the team, managing vendors, setting operational strategy, and driving problem and change management.

Key Responsibilities:
Network Infrastructure Management (Core Routing and Switching):
- Own the operational health, performance, and security of the core routing and switching environment across datacenter, campus, WAN edge, and cloud connectivity, built primarily on Cisco platforms (e.g., Nexus, Catalyst, ISR/ASR)
- Oversee the design, implementation, and maintenance of resilient WAN and LAN networks to ensure high availability, performance, and security
- Manage routing and switching operations — BGP, OSPF/EIGRP, VLANs, spanning tree, VXLAN/EVPN, VRFs, QoS, and access control — including turn-ups, changes, and remediation

Core Network Services (DNS / DHCP / IPAM):
- Operate and safeguard DNS (Domain Name System), DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol), and IPAM services using Infoblox for reliable name resolution and address management across the enterprise
- Maintain supporting services such as NTP and network authentication (e.g., RADIUS / 802.1X) in partnership with identity and security teams

SDN, SD-WAN, and Connectivity:
- Implement and oversee software-defined networking and SD-WAN capabilities (Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN and ACI) to enhance network agility, efficiency, and scalability
- Manage connectivity to multi-cloud environments and coordinate carrier / WAN services

Network Monitoring:
- Ensure network device monitoring is captured, acknowledged, and reported, and streamline monitoring into a single-pane-of-glass view

WellTheory is a digital health company helping people with autoimmune conditions take control of their health through personalized care, nutrition guidance, and ongoing coaching. We're a team of 60+ passionate people who care deeply about helping our members reduce symptoms, feel better, and live fuller lives — while helping employers and payors reduce their spend.




ABOUT THE ROLE

WellTheory is hiring its first Head of Engineering.

You’ll lead a talented, largely self-directed team and set how we build: our process, our quality bar, our technical direction, and who we hire. This is a player-coach role; Expect to spend 20-30% of your time in the codebase and the rest leading the team, shaping the platform, and partnering with product, design, and leadership. You’ll report to our Co-Founder & Chief Product Officer.

We’re a Series A company operating like a much bigger one. We build the member app, in-house tools for our Care Team, and the insurance and data infrastructure that connects us to employers, health plans, and channel partners, all with HIPAA and SOC 2 Type 2 in mind.

We’re looking for a leader who has seen scale before, knows what to build now so we don’t have to rebuild later, and can empower experienced, high-achieving engineers.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Build and grow the team. Run 1:1s, set a high bar, and own hiring, performance, and career growth.

 - Define how we ship. Design planning, code review, testing, release, and incident practices that are fast enough for a small AI-native team and rigorous enough for compliance.

 - Set technical direction. Make the foundational architecture calls with our founding engineer, so velocity holds as we scale the team and member base.

 - Own platform and DevOps. Set the roadmap, including non-prod environments that keep PHI out of day-to-day development.

 - Build compliance in, not on. Work with ops and compliance leads on the engineering side of HIPAA, SOC 2, and HITRUST.

 - Make AI core to how we build. Roll out coding agents, evals, and internal tooling that multiply every engineer’s impact.

 - Stay hands-on. Review code, pair on the hard problems, and ship when it’s the highest-leverage use of your time.

 - Shape the roadmap. Partner with our Staff PM and Product Design Lead on scope and tradeoffs.

 - Speak for engineering. Represent the team at the leadership table.



YOU MIGHT BE A GREAT FIT IF YOU...

 - Have led engineering teams through growth. You’ve managed senior ICs, built teams, and know what breaks at each stage and what to fix first.

 - Have built in a regulated environment. Healthcare, fintech, or another industry where data handling, security, and audits shape how you build. You treat compliance as table stakes, not a blocker.

 - Spot great talent. You can tell great from good in an interview or code review, and you hire for potential.

 - Stay hands-on. You’ve shipped production TypeScript or JavaScript recently and want to keep doing it.

Director, Cloud Infrastructure

We're hiring a Director of Cloud Infrastructure to join Convene Hospitality Group's (CHG) Technology organization. It's a hands-on role with an AI-native mindset. There are no direct reports today. Job Classification:
Technology - Architecture

Data and Artificial Intelligence are rapidly becoming foundational capabilities that will transform how Prudential builds software, operates platforms, serves customers, empowers employees, and creates business value.

Prudential is seeking a Vice President, Enterprise Data & AI Architect to help define and build the future of Data and AI across the enterprise. Reporting to the Chief Architect, this highly visible leadership role sits at the intersection of enterprise architecture, data architecture, AI strategy, platform engineering, and business transformation.

The position plays a unique role in Prudential’s technology leadership model, connecting Enterprise Architecture and the Chief Data & AI Office to help ensure a unified approach to enterprise data, AI strategy, platforms, governance, and execution. We are looking for a leader who combines strategic vision with deep technical expertise and a passion for staying at the forefront of innovation. Prudential is actively investing in strategic Data & AI accelerators focused on transforming how we build software, operate platforms, empower employees, serve customers, and grow the business. The successful candidate will help lead the architectural evolution of these capabilities, ensuring that innovations such as modern data platforms, Generative AI, AI Assistants, Agentic AI, and emerging human + AI operating models translate into scalable enterprise solutions that deliver measurable business value. Success will require balancing innovation with the realities of a large global enterprise. The successful candidate will help Prudential unlock value from modern data and AI capabilities while navigating an environment that includes mainframe platforms, multiple systems of record, complex identity resolution challenges, and decades of critical business data.

Your Team & Role
As a member of both the Enterprise Architecture Leadership Team and the Chief Data & AI Office (CDAIO) Leadership Team, this leader helps ensure Prudential’s data architecture, AI strategy, platforms, and governance evolve as a unified enterprise capability.

**Have you trained AI models for materials and shown a measured uplift? Join as co-founder and CTO.**

A seed-stage AI-for-materials company in New York turns unpublished lab data from academia into new, synthesizable materials. Its seed round is closing. As co-founder and CTO you'd own the AI engineering and the data-and-discovery engine, and build the team after the round. For a top builder who isn't ready for co-founder risk, there is also a founding-engineer track.

**What you'll own**

* The AI engineering behind materials discovery, end to end
* The data-and-discovery engine: data, architecture and measured uplift
* Building and leading the engineering team after the seed

**Must-haves**

* You've built, trained and deployed AI models for materials (AI for biology or protein-structure work doesn't count here)
* You build a model end to end, from data to architecture to measured uplift, and you're strong on data pipelines, not research only
* You use frontier models in your work
* 4+ years of real industry experience (roughly 4–10)
* In person in New York, 9-9-6

**Bonus points**

* A materials model with a measured uplift from data you collected yourself
* AI-for-science work at a leading lab, a commercial PhD or postdoc, or an AI-materials startup
* A network you can recruit from

**What's in it for you**

* $120k–$500k base + 1–20% equity, depending on the track
* A co-founder seat at the start of a new company

**Good to know**

* Full-time, in person in New York, 9-9-6
* Sponsorship is limited: please tell us your exact work authorization up front
Process: screening with the CEO technical conversation take-home (a theory problem, 24 hours) with a follow-up final technical round with an advisor (coding challenge plus a deep conversation) a work trial of about a week in New York* offer

**When you apply, please include**

* Your CV (PDF), your **LinkedIn URL**, and GitHub or papers if you have them
* The materials model you built, and the uplift it delivered
* Whether you're interested in the co-founder (CTO) track or the founding-engineer track
* Your current location, and confirmation that in person in New York works for you
* Your visa or citizenship status, and if you'll need sponsorship
* Your base salary expectation, your notice period, and any other interview processes you're in

Does this sound like you? Apply now. If you're a match, we'll be in touch within 3 working days.

You will be part of a team building Bain’s integrated suite of agentic decisioning tools that gives large organizations always-on intelligence across their most important growth decisions. The Senior Director, Digital Capability and Workforce Modernization owns our Company approach to redesigning work for a Human × AI enterprise and building the digital and AI capability people need to perform that work. Set the Enterprise Approach to Workforce and Workflow Modernization

###### **About Us**

Founded in 2015 to develop the world’s first industrially scalable laser metal additive manufacturing solution, VulcanForms is reshaping how the world manufactures critical products. We build and operate advanced digital infrastructure that enables innovation, accelerates growth, and supports sustainability across aerospace, defense, medical, and other essential industries. Through our vertically integrated capabilities, including scalable additive manufacturing and precision machining, we deliver true end-to-end production at scale by combining cutting-edge technology with a foundation of proven industrial craftsmanship. Our team brings deep expertise in manufacturing, materials science, software, automation, and operations, united by a shared commitment to quality, curiosity, and accountability. We foster an inclusive culture where people take ownership, solve meaningful problems, and continuously learn, because we believe diverse perspectives lead to better outcomes.

The Director of Engineering, leads the engineering organization that takes new customer programs from first article to stable, repeatable production. You will own the New Product Introduction process end to end. That covers design for additive manufacturing (DFAM), build and process development, post-processing and machining, qualification, and handoff to production. Schedule, cost, and quality commitments must be met throughout. We are looking for a hands-on technical leader who can build and develop a high-performing team, set the standards for how VulcanForms introduces new products, and serve as a trusted engineering partner to customers, Commercial, Operations, and Quality.

###### **Key Responsibilities**

* Lead, hire, and develop a team of NPI engineers and engineering managers across process development, manufacturing engineering, and program execution.
* Own the NPI process from customer handoff through production release, including stage gates, readiness reviews, and clear criteria for transfer to production.
* Drive DFAM, build layout, and process parameter development to deliver parts that meet customer requirements for geometry, material properties, surface finish, and cost.
* Integrate the full digital manufacturing workflow, including printing, thermal processing, part removal, precision machining, finishing, and inspection, into robust, documented manufacturing processes.
* Lead first article inspection, process qualification, and customer qualification activities, partnering with Quality to meet aerospace, defense, and other industry requirements.
* Make data-driven engineering decisions using DOE, SPC, root cause analysis, and process capability studies, and hold the team to a high standard of technical rigor.
* Serve as the senior engineering point of contact for key customers during NPI, setting expectations, communicating risks and tradeoffs, and building long-term trust.
* Partner with Commercial and Applications

**Company Overview**

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. Solutions forged from experience; that is how we build, and it is how we hire.

**Job Summary**
===============

Orbis is hiring a Vice President of Engineering to lead our engineering organization through its most significant period of growth. You will lead our engineering directors and managers, hire and develop an exceptional technical workforce, and shape a culture where engineers do their best work while the organization triples in size over the next year.

You will report directly to the CTO and serve as the senior engineering leader accountable for how Orbis builds: the people, the leaders, the culture, the delivery engine, and the engineering standards. The CTO sets technical vision and architecture direction; you own the organization and operating model that turns that vision into reliable delivery at scale.

This role is built for a leader who has done it before in a small, fast-moving company, and who can bring structure without bureaucracy. You will be a visible, trusted voice with engineers, executives, and government customers alike. * **Own delivery and accountability.** Partner with product leadership to turn priorities into predictable delivery, balancing roadmap commit

Kairos Power is a new nuclear energy technology and engineering company whose mission is to enable the world’s transition to clean energy, with the ultimate goal to dramatically improve people’s quality of life while protecting the environment. Job Summary

The Senior Director of Power Plant Engineering is the senior technical and organizational leader accountable for the technical adequacy, maturity, integration, and execution of the designs produced by the Power Plant Engineering organization. Reporting to the Vice President of Engineering Design, this position holds final design decision authority for the Power Plant Engineering organization.

The position ensures that the organization produces technically sound, mature, coordinated, and executable designs that meet established plant requirements, design criteria, codes and standards, safety objectives, and program commitments. This is a working senior leadership role requiring hands-on technical experience and active engagement. The Senior Director establishes technical direction, assigns clear decision authority within the organization, and ensures that consequential engineering decisions have an adequate technical basis and are made by qualified decision-makers. The Senior Director holds leaders accountable while personally engaging in consequential technical decisions, design reviews, issue resolution, and recovery of critical engineering work when necessary.

- Establish technical direction, maintain engineering standards, and ensure consistent execution of high-quality engineering products in accordance with the Design Control Program and systems engineering practices established by Design Assurance.
- Ensure that system and discipline designs satisfy applicable requirements, codes and standards, safety functions, and are aligned with program objectives.
- Ensure that design assumptions, margins, uncertainties, limitations, and technical risks are identified, documented, communicated, and appropriately managed.
- Make or approve technical decisions and accept technical risk within delegated authority.
- Hold senior technical leaders accountable for the technical quality, maturity, timeliness, and completeness of their organizations’ work.
- Resolve technical disagreements that cross system or discipline boundaries.
- Ensure that Power Plant Engineering provides technically complete and timely inputs to plant layout, process design, plan

HEAD OF IT

Freeform builds AI-native manufacturing systems that unify software, hardware, and physics to produce industrial-scale parts at the speed of human ideation. By treating manufacturing as a single integrated system, we unlock a new era of innovation where complex hardware is designed, built, and scaled without limits.

In this role, you will report directly to the CEO and own the technology infrastructure behind Freeform: the data centers and cloud platforms that run our factories, the networks and security that protect them, and the corporate IT that keeps our people productive. You will set the IT strategy and be accountable to the executive team for uptime, security, and compliance. Your most immediate priority is the infrastructure and dedicated data center for our new manufacturing facility, which becomes the blueprint as we deploy factories around the world. The many petabytes of data our factories generate are a core advantage, and the systems that capture, store, and protect it are part of the product.

All leadership roles at Freeform are technical in nature. You will spend a significant portion of your time hands-on, making architecture calls, reviewing designs, and building alongside the team while you run

Responsibilities:
- Set the IT and infrastructure strategy and roadmap, tied to Freeform’s factory expansion, and present it to the executive team
- Architect, build, and commission the infrastructure and dedicated data center for our new facility, including power, cooling, compute, storage, network, and edge-compute on the factory floor, as a repeatable blueprint for future factories
- Own storage and compute for petabyte-scale physics and process data, including high-bandwidth interconnects
- Own the Kubernetes and virtualization platforms, on-prem and in the cloud
- Own network architecture across all sites, including segmentation between corporate, server, OT, and guest zones
- Build and run the security program: controls, monitoring, incident response, audits, and vulnerability management
- Own compliance with NIST 800-171, CMMC, and ITAR, and serve as the point of accountability for IT-related audits and customer security reviews
- Ensure high availability, disaster recovery, and business continuity for systems that drive production
- Run corporate IT alongside engineering infrastructure, including identity and access, endpoints, and collaboration tools
- Own the IT budget and make the build-vs-buy and on-prem-vs-cloud calls that keep infrastructure cost-efficient as we scale
- Select and manage vendors, hardware suppliers, and cloud providers, and set IT policies, standards, and change management
- Report on availability, risk, and security posture to executive leadership
- Stay hands-on: review designs, make architecture calls, and build and troubleshoot alongside the team
- Lead and mentor the IT team, and plan, hire, and build the organization as Freeform scales, setting its priorities and a culture of ownership

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Maritime Manufacturing Technology Team is responsible for rapidly developing and implementing manufacturing technologies, processes, and materials for cutting-edge defense hardware. The team is developing deployable static and moving surface, undersea and sea to air vehicles, and scaling these products in our new manufacturing facilities.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a Head of Production to join our team in Santa Ana, CA to stand up a cutting-edge manufacturing site. This role is crucial in ensuring that each initiative aligns with the company's strategic direction and receives the appropriate resourcing, balancing innovation with practical execution to drive the business line's success. You will build and lead the product line organization from scratch, establishing and managing manufacturing processes, quality systems, and the infrastructure needed to scale from prototype builds through full-rate production.

As a leader in the Maritime Division, you must bear the expertise to evaluate, qualify, manage, and advocate for an increasing number of sophisticated parallel pursuits. Your spectrum of support will be exceptionally diverse and require you to rapidly drive aggressive deliverables to completion.

The ideal candidate will leverage a deep expertise in large-scale manufacturing of a number of large, complex assemblies. You need to have experience in heavy fabrication, be able to lead the complex integration of different structures, and have a background spanning structural fabrication, joining and assembly across a variety of metals, alloys, and exotic materials. You need to have led an organization of hundreds, not dozens, and come from an operation comparable to the scale we are building at Anduril. You are a builder, not a caretaker.

WHAT YOU’LL DO
- Own all production activity: manufacturing and production support.
- Build and lead the production organization, supporting hiring across manufacturing engineering, quality, and operations.
- Establish manufacturing processes and production infrastructure for complex electromechanical vehicles.
- Drive NPI and the manufacturing development lifecycle: Concept, Prototype, LRIP, FRP.
- Manage production budgets, schedules, and on-time delivery performance.

JLL empowers you to shape a brighter way .

Our people at JLL are shaping the future of real estate for a better world by combining world class services, advisory and technology for our clients. We are committed to hiring the best, most talented people and empowering them to thrive, grow meaningful careers and to find a place where they belong.  Whether you’ve got deep experience in commercial real estate, skilled trades or technology, or you’re looking to apply your relevant experience to a new industry, join our team as we help shape a brighter way forward.

About JLL
We’re JLL. We’re a professional services and investment management firm specializing in real estate. We help organizations around the world achieve their ambitions by owning, occupying and investing in real estate.

As a business of around 92,000 people in more than 80 countries, with many more contractors and vendors working under our direction, JLL’s Corporate Solutions business has substantial and diverse Health, Safety, Security and Environment (HSSE) responsibilities and obligations. These apply in our own workplaces and in the portfolio of client space we manage.

If you’re looking to step up your career, JLL is the perfect professional home. At JLL, you’ll have a chance to innovate with the world’s leading businesses, put that expertise into action on landmark projects, and work on game-changing real estate initiatives. You’ll also make long-lasting professional connections through sharing different perspectives, and you’ll be inspired by the best. We’re focused on opportunity and want to help you make the most of yours. Achieve your ambitions – join us at JLL!

Role Purpose
The North American Physical Security Director will manage the development and implementation of an effective security service delivery program to mitigate risk, safeguard the accounts human assets, intellectual property, integrity, reputation, and physical assets to ensure continuity of operations in the North American region. The role will liasie with various stakeholders and provide governance and assurance of the in scope programme and assist the clients security management team in the regional security program.  The role’s primary objectives will be to manage third party security guard contracts and provide operational assurance and delivery of KPI’s and SLA’s.  The role address all aspects of physical & personnnel security within the scope of the contract, incident & crisis management, emergency preparedness and response, investigations, security education and training, contingency planning, administrative security. The Security Director will report to the Americas JLL account Regional Account Director/Customer Relationship Manager (CRM) and will also function as the account Global Security SME, and work closely with other Regional Account Director CRMs, Regional JLL P&G Account Security Teams, Corporate JLL Security Platform Lead and Client Global Security Lead.

The Director Solution Architect, Hyperscale Power serves as Vertiv's primary technical partner for an assigned strategic hyperscale customer, working directly with the customer’s engineering organization providing design assistance to current and next-generation power infrastructure architectures enabling best in class engineered solution from creation to deployment.

Aligned one-to-one with a strategic customer, the Solution Architect develops a deep understanding of the customer's technology roadmap, design standards, operating requirements, and future infrastructure strategies, and drives alignment with Vertiv product development requirements. The Director, Data Center Planning & Scheduling will lead the client planning and scheduling function for a construction campus comprising multiple data centers and shared infrastructure. Manage a team of planners and schedulers to establish integrated schedules, assess delivery performance, identify emerging risks, and provide clear advice to client leadership.

Provide oversight and challenge of contractor schedules, ensuring that campus priorities, building completion dates, infrastructure readiness, commissioning, and operational handover are aligned.

This role requires 50% travel.

Director, Data Center Planning & Scheduling - Santa Teresa, NM
Key responsibilities
Team leadership
- Lead, develop, and coordinate a team of planners and schedulers across multiple buildings, infrastructure packages, and delivery phases.
- Allocate resources to match project priorities and maintain consistent planning standards, methods, and reporting.
- Review the quality of team deliverables and provide technical guidance on scheduling, analysis, and forecasting.
- Establish clear ownership of schedule interfaces and coordination with contractors and client stakeholders.

Integrated planning and scheduling
- Develop and maintain the client’s integrated campus master schedule, incorporating design, permitting, procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover.
- Coordinate dependencies between individual data centers and shared infrastructure, including power, utilities, communications, access, and logistics.
- Integrate long-lead equipment manufacturing, delivery, installation, and testing milestones into the overall delivery plan.
- Establish schedule baselines, milestone definitions, progress measurement requirements, and schedule update procedures.
- Evaluate contractor baseline schedules, updates, recovery plans, and proposed changes for completeness, credibility, and alignment with client requirements.
- Coordinate phased turnover and commissioning sequences with client operations and relevant technical teams.

CPM and schedule assurance
- Apply strong Critical Path Method (CPM) expertise to assess schedule logic, activity durations, calendars, constraints, float, and critical and near-critical paths.
- Assess whether schedules accurately represent construction methods, sequencing, interfaces, and completion requirements.
- Identify open-ended activities, excessive constraints, inappropriate lags, and other weaknesses affecting forecast reliability.
- Challenge unsupported assumptions and assess the practicality of proposed mitigation, acceleration, and recovery measures.
- Maintain visibility of the drivers of campus and building completion dates.

Trending, analytics, and forecasting
- Establish schedule performance indicators and dashboards that support timely client decisions.
- Analyze milestone movement, float erosion, critical path changes, progress variance, productivity, and procurement performance.
- Identify adverse trends across reporting
